questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which of the following function pairs will cause a compilation error due to ambiguous overloading when called with `foo(5)`?

options.A: void foo(int x); and void foo(double x);
options.B: void foo(int x); and void foo(int x, int y = 10);
options.C: void foo(int x); and void foo(std::string x);
options.D: void foo(int x); and void foo(int x, int y);

questions.explanation: Calling foo(5) is ambiguous because it matches both void foo(int) and void foo(int, int = 10).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is an initializer list in a C++ constructor used for?

options.A: To initialize member variables directly before the constructor body executes
options.C: To initialize local variables inside methods

questions.explanation: Constructor member initializer lists initialize class data members directly prior to constructor body execution.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is dynamic dispatch in C++?

options.A: Resolving function calls at compile time
options.B: Resolving virtual function calls at runtime based on the actual object type

questions.explanation: Dynamic dispatch resolves polymorphic virtual function calls at runtime via vtable mechanism.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the primary function of the vptr (virtual pointer) in C++ objects with virtual functions?

options.A: Points to heap memory allocated for class
options.B: Points to the Virtual Method Table (vtable) for the object's class

questions.explanation: Objects of classes with virtual functions contain a hidden pointer (vptr) pointing to the class's vtable.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: When is a copy constructor invoked in C++?

options.A: When an object is initialized with another object of the same class
options.B: When an object is passed by value to a function
options.C: When a function returns an object by value

questions.explanation: Copy constructors are called when initializing an object from another instance, passing by value, or returning by value.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the correct syntax to declare a generic function template in C++?

options.A: template <typename T> T maxVal(T a, T b);
options.B: generic <class T> T maxVal(T a, T b);
options.C: template <T> T maxVal(T a, T b);
options.D: type <template T> T maxVal(T a, T b);

questions.explanation: 'template <typename T>' or 'template <class T>' declares a function template.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What happens if an exception is thrown in C++ but not caught by any matching catch block in the call stack?

options.B: std::terminate() is called automatically, ending execution

questions.explanation: Uncaught exceptions cause the runtime to call std::terminate() (which calls std::abort()).

questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: STL containers (vector, list, deque, set, map, unordered_map)
questions.question: What is the underlying data structure and search time complexity of std::map in standard C++?

options.B: Red-Black Tree (balanced BST) with O(log N) time

questions.explanation: std::map is typically implemented as a self-balancing Red-Black tree providing logarithmic O(log N) operations.

questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: STL containers (vector, list, deque, set, map, unordered_map)
questions.question: What is the difference between std::map and std::unordered_map?

options.A: std::map is sorted O(log N); std::unordered_map is hash-based O(1) average time
options.B: std::map uses hashing; std::unordered_map uses BST
options.C: std::unordered_map allows duplicate keys; std::map does not

questions.explanation: std::map maintains sorted keys using trees (O(log N)), whereas std::unordered_map uses hash tables (O(1) average).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: In C++11 lambda `[=](int x) { return x + a; }`, what does `[=]` signify?

options.A: Capture all outer local variables by value
options.B: Capture all outer local variables by reference

questions.explanation: The [=] capture default captures outer local variables used in the lambda body by value.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: In C++ lambda `[&](int x) { return x + a; }`, what does `[&]` signify?
questions.explanation: The [&] capture default captures outer variables by reference.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which standard stream class is used for reading input from a file in C++?
questions.explanation: std::ifstream (input file stream) is used for reading files.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Quick Sort algorithm?
questions.explanation: Quick sort degrades to O(N^2) in worst-case scenarios when pivot selection is unbalanced.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which of the following C++ operators CANNOT be overloaded?
questions.explanation: The scope resolution operator ::, member access operator ., direct pointer-to-member .*, and ternary operator ?: cannot be overloaded.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: When overloading operator+ as a non-member friend function taking two parameters (A, B), what is the correct declaration?

options.A: friend MyClass operator+(const MyClass& a, const MyClass& b);

questions.explanation: A non-member binary operator overload takes two arguments corresponding to left and right operands.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which algorithm header function searches for a value in a sorted range using binary search?
questions.explanation: std::binary_search checks if an element exists in a sorted range in O(log N) time.

questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: Stack, queue, linked list, and tree fundamentals
questions.question: Which STL container adapter implements First-In, First-Out (FIFO) behavior?
questions.explanation: std::queue provides FIFO (First-In, First-Out) operations.

questions.subject: C++
questions.explanation: Test::count is incremented by each constructor call. Creating 3 objects sets count to 3.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is a dangling pointer in C++?

options.B: A pointer pointing to a memory location that has been deallocated

questions.explanation: A dangling pointer stores the memory address of an object that has been freed or destroyed.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What happens if you call `delete` on a pointer allocated with `new[]`?

options.A: Only the first element's destructor is called; undefined behavior occurs

questions.explanation: Mismatching new[] with scalar delete causes undefined behavior (destructors for array elements 1..N-1 are skipped).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is an abstract class in C++?

options.A: A class with no member variables
options.B: A class containing at least one pure virtual function
options.D: A class that cannot have subclasses

questions.explanation: A class with at least one pure virtual function (virtual void foo() = 0;) is abstract and cannot be instantiated.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which keyword in C++11 explicitly specifies that a member function is intended to override a base class virtual function?
questions.explanation: The 'override' specifier verifies that a function overrides a base class virtual method at compile time.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which specifier in C++11 prevents a virtual function from being overridden in derived classes?
questions.explanation: The 'final' specifier prevents further overriding of a virtual function or inheritance of a class.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which smart pointer in C++11 owns an object uniquely and prevents copy assignment?
questions.explanation: std::unique_ptr represents exclusive ownership; it cannot be copied, only moved.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which smart pointer is used to break cyclic reference dependencies created by std::shared_ptr?
questions.explanation: std::weak_ptr holds a non-owning reference to an object managed by std::shared_ptr without incrementing reference count.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question:
What does a 'const' qualifier after a member function signature specify?
`void display() const;`

options.A: The function returns a constant value
options.B: The function cannot modify non-mutable data members of the object
options.C: The function cannot be called on const objects

questions.explanation: Const member functions promise not to alter non-mutable member variables of the calling object.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which keyword allows a class member variable to be modified inside a const member function?
questions.explanation: Members declared 'mutable' can be modified even within const member functions.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the correct syntax to declare a pure virtual function in C++?
questions.explanation: 'virtual ReturnType FunctionName() = 0;' declares a pure virtual function.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is shallow copy versus deep copy in classes managing dynamic memory?

options.A: Shallow copy copies pointers directly (sharing memory); deep copy allocates new memory and copies contents
options.B: Deep copy copies pointers; shallow copy allocates memory
options.C: Shallow copy is for references; deep copy is for pointers

questions.explanation: Shallow copying duplicates raw pointer addresses leading to shared state; deep copying creates distinct heap resources.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which STL container provides constant time O(1) insertions/deletions at both ends?
questions.explanation: std::deque (double-ended queue) supports O(1) push and pop at both head and tail.

questions.subject: C++
questions.explanation: ref is an alias for 'a'. Assigning ref = b assigns 20 to 'a', leaving a=20 and b=20.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which standard exception class in <stdexcept> is thrown when memory allocation fails with `new`?
questions.explanation: When dynamic memory allocation fails, operator new throws std::bad_alloc.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the result of calling std::advance(it, 3) on an iterator 'it'?

options.B: Returns a new iterator 3 positions ahead without modifying 'it'

questions.explanation: std::advance modifies the passed iterator in-place by advancing it N steps.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which C++ casting operator is used for safe downcasting in polymorphic class hierarchies at runtime?
questions.explanation: dynamic_cast safely converts pointers/references within class hierarchies using RTTI.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which casting operator removes const or volatile qualifiers from a variable?
questions.explanation: const_cast is explicitly designed to cast away constness or volatility.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the space complexity of a recursive implementation of depth N due to call stack memory?
questions.explanation: Recursion of depth N allocates N stack frames, consuming O(N) auxiliary space.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the average time complexity of Merge Sort?
questions.explanation: Merge sort guarantees O(N log N) time complexity in best, average, and worst cases.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What does RAII stand for in C++ core software engineering?
questions.explanation: RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) ties resource lifetime to object scope/destruction.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the purpose of `std::move` from <utility> in C++11?

options.A: Physically moves memory bytes across RAM
options.B: Unconditionally casts an lvalue to an rvalue reference, enabling move semantics

questions.explanation: std::move casts an expression to an rvalue reference (T&&) allowing resource transfer.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is template specialization in C++?

options.A: Providing a custom implementation of a template for a specific data type

questions.explanation: Template specialization defines tailored implementations for specific template argument types.

questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: Stack, queue, linked list, and tree fundamentals
questions.question: In a Binary Search Tree (BST), which traversal visits nodes in ascending sorted order?
questions.explanation: In-order traversal (Left, Root, Right) processes BST nodes in sorted ascending order.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What method is used to close an open file stream in C++?
questions.explanation: close() flushes stream buffers and detaches the stream from the file.

questions.subject: C++

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: How do you define a custom namespace named 'Physics' in C++?
questions.explanation: 'namespace Physics { ... }' defines a scoped namespace.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is `constexpr` introduced in C++11?

options.A: Specifies that expression/function can be evaluated at compile time
options.B: Makes variable constant at runtime only

questions.explanation: constexpr guarantees compile-time evaluation for constant expressions and functions.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What type of error is caused by accessing `vec[10]` on std::vector `vec` of size 5 using `vec.at(10)`?
questions.explanation: The at() method performs bounds checking and throws std::out_of_range on invalid index access.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which method removes the last element of std::vector in C++?
questions.explanation: pop_back() removes the last element and decreases vector size by 1.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: In what order are object destructors called relative to their constructor invocation order in automatic scope?
questions.explanation: Objects on the stack are destroyed in strict reverse order of construction (LIFO).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Can a derived class access private members of its base class directly?

options.B: No, private base members are inaccessible to derived classes directly

questions.explanation: Private members of a base class are preserved private and inaccessible directly by derived classes.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is 'this' pointer in C++ member functions?

options.A: A pointer to the current object instance calling the non-static member function

questions.explanation: The 'this' pointer is an implicit parameter passed to non-static member functions pointing to the invoking object.
